summary: Modoc County, CA steel lookout tower on Tulelake NWR, built about 1937; sources disagree on height and which tower stood there; now gone, a concrete pad remains.

facts.design: Aermotor open steel tower with a 7x7 observation cabin, 80 ft per the register; a 1937 newspaper describes a 100 ft all-steel tower topped by a small steel house
facts.status_note: A concrete pad is all that remains at the site; removal date unknown

events.note: Register says constructed circa 1937; a January 1937 newspaper says CCC crews from the Clear Lake camp had just completed the all-steel tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 80 feet; the January 1937 newspaper gives 100 feet for the new steel tower. Neither is chosen, so height_m is left unset.

The register describes an Aermotor open steel tower with a 7x7 cabin; the 1937 newspaper describes an all-steel tower topped by a small steel house and does not name Aermotor. Both descriptions are kept in facts.design.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on height (80 ft register vs 100 ft 1937 press) and design wording. The sequence of 1937-38 towers is unresolved, so no 1938 event is recorded for this site; the July 1938 report describes a moved and rebuilt tower plus a second new one at the peninsula, and a May 1937 report describes the headquarters tower being moved to Upper Klamath Lake; no source says which tower became the register's tower, so the story flags this. The brief's 1937 build date is supported. A 1940 memo about a water tower for the peninsula cabin is not about the lookout and was left out. The register's 1964 photo credit (courtesy Tulelake NWR Headquarters) has no image URL, so no photo entry. No access information found; the story says so.
